### Counts behind Section I's catalog sentence

- Aggregation-level entries: 9 (#7, #8, #9, #13, #16, #17, #18, #25, #27); caught only by a later independent pass or review: **8** (#7, #8, #9, #13, #16, #17, #18, #27); caught by a pre-registered test: **1** (#25).
- Entries caught by a pre-registered test inside their own gate (all families): **4** (#10, #21, #25, #30); of them aggregation-level: 1.
- Catalog text on the aggregation family (`ARTIFACT_CATALOG.md`, 'Scope of the observation'): among aggregation entries that reached a reported figure or conclusion (#7, #8, #9, #13, #16, #17, #18) every one was caught by an independent pass or review; #25 is the one aggregation entry caught inside its own gate, by a pre-registered prediction.
- **Assessment of Section I's sentence** ("errors arising from a mismatch of aggregation level ... were caught only by later, independent passes, after they had spread into other reports, whereas pre-registered predictions caught errors inside the gate that made them"): the first half is supported for the seven aggregation entries that reached a reported result (#7, #8, #9, #13, #16, #17, #18; #27 was caught by a later gate's author and no wrong number reached a report). "After they had spread into other reports" is documented for #13 (every oracle result for 103 days) and not for each of the seven in the catalog text. The second half is supported only in part: pre-registered tests caught 4 entries inside their own gate, one of which (#25) is aggregation-level, and the catalog states that the sample behind each mechanism is small (n = 2-3) and that in-gate catches are under-counted by construction (selection effect). **The sentence as written overstates a contrast the catalog itself calls descriptive**; this is a disagreement for the author, not edited here.
